scope: Future /tree contract sketch and current-core fit, with /graph boundary; no implementation or publication

conclusion.boundedTo: Rooted ordered trees with immutable valid endpoint snapshots, explicit link identities, atomic topology changes and scene composition; no automatic layout or algorithm implementation
conclusion.graphBoundary: The initial graph trace remains fixed-topology; changing tree states use generic playback/scene, not a widened graph contract

requirements.model: One root (or empty), ordered children, one parent per nonroot, connected and acyclic, stable node/link IDs
requirements.identity: Namespaced scene IDs; retain entity identity across hierarchy/layout changes; trace allocation rules require later API design
requirements.validity: Tree module validates atomic updates before commit; generic Scene intentionally has no tree validator
requirements.transitions: Use both previous/current link references and scene.get for changed or exiting endpoints
requirements.projection: Pure immutable endpoint projection; layout and viewport policies stay separate from playback
requirements.persistentResult: Store marks and result in State, not accumulated events/render history
requirements.moduleBoundary: Headless DOM-free model; optional rendering and graph interop still require separate API design

runtimeProbe.scope: Existing core with handwritten application snapshots; no future /tree or /graph implementation

checks.name: Empty tree needs no core sentinel scene object
Equal labels do not merge node identities
Tree, graph and link namespaces compose without collision
Rotation matches retained nodes by ID, not root/depth/order
Changing root is application state, not a Scene field
Ordered siblings remain opaque snapshot data
Retargeted link preserves both old and new endpoint references
Both endpoint generations resolve through scene.get
Shared progress interpolates moved root and child
Tree event and non-positional source index survive Scene matching
Subtree removal exposes old node and incident links together
Disappearing link can resolve a deleted endpoint
Insertion exposes new nodes and links at the same progress
New identity with the same label produces enter and exit
Graph and tree handlers coexist in one generic registry
Existing layer ordering puts tree links before tree nodes
Pure projector caches immutable endpoints, not event or progress
Reverse frame keeps hierarchy and geometry from both snapshots
Empty tree can be a valid initial playback state
Seek and terminal hold preserve selected result state
Seeking may skip topology changes without losing current scene
Terminal predicate closes tree source once without EOF lookahead
Fresh source restores original root and clears result

State-only sources need no tree event to retain result
Generic Scene deliberately does not validate tree acyclicity
Existing same-ID type validation still applies
Current tree example retains application pointer routing
Existing heap already projects synchronized tree/array identities
Plain tree state is structured-cloneable

typeProbe.scope: Application-only tree types against existing core/widget, no package declarations added

existingRegressionChecks.notes: Existing SVG test uses a test DOM; not native browser evidence. Heap corpus reports 1403 inputs.
